title: What GPU Does the PS5 Have? Specs and PC Equivalent
h1: What GPU Does the PS5 Have?
query: what gpu does the ps5 have
description: The PS5 has a custom AMD RDNA 2 GPU: 36 CUs at up to 2.23 GHz, 10.28 TFLOPS, 448 GB/s. It is roughly a desktop RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super. Specs inside.
dek: The graphics chip inside the PlayStation 5, from Sony's published specs: what it is, how powerful it is, and the desktop graphics card it is closest to.
quickAnswer: The PS5 has a custom AMD GPU based on RDNA 2, the architecture of the Radeon RX 6000 series. It has 36 compute units at up to 2.23 GHz for 10.28 TFLOPS, and shares 16 GB of GDDR6 at 448 GB/s with the CPU. On PC, it is roughly a Radeon RX 6700 or GeForce RTX 2070 Super, and an RTX 4060, RTX 5060 or Arc B580 matches or slightly beats it.
intro: The PS5's graphics are not a separate card. Sony and AMD built them into one custom chip, an APU, alongside an 8-core AMD Zen 2 CPU, and both share the same 16 GB pool of GDDR6 memory. Sony published the key numbers in Mark Cerny's Road to PS5 presentation: 36 RDNA 2 compute units, a variable clock of up to 2.23 GHz, 10.28 TFLOPS, and 448 GB/s of memory bandwidth.

Every PS5 model has that same GPU: the original 2020 console, the Digital Edition, and the smaller PS5 Slim. This page explains what those specs mean, how powerful the GPU is, and which desktop graphics card it matches. The PC matches are rough, widely reported equivalents built from the published specs and from independent console-versus-PC comparisons. We have not tested the console.

sections.h: The PS5 GPU: Custom AMD RDNA 2 With 36 Compute Units
body: The PS5's GPU is made by AMD, not NVIDIA. It uses AMD's RDNA 2 architecture, the same generation as the desktop Radeon RX 6000 series and the Xbox Series X. Sony calls it a custom design: AMD supplied the graphics cores, and Sony chose the size, clock behaviour and a few additions of its own, such as cache scrubbers tied to the fast SSD.

It has 36 compute units, each with 64 shaders, for 2,304 shaders in total. RDNA 2 includes hardware ray tracing, so the PS5 has one ray accelerator per compute unit, the same arrangement as an RX 6000 card. That is enough for ray-traced reflections and shadows in many games, though it is the weakest part of the GPU next to NVIDIA cards.

The clock is variable. Instead of a fixed frequency, the PS5 runs on a fixed power budget and lets the CPU and GPU clocks move within it. The GPU runs at up to 2.23 GHz and, by Sony's description, stays at or close to that most of the time, dropping a little only in the heaviest scenes. At 2.23 GHz, 36 compute units give the 10.28 TFLOPS figure Sony quotes.

sections.h: How Powerful Is the PS5 GPU?
body: The PS5 GPU is a capable mid-range graphics chip by today's standards. It was close to high-end PC graphics at launch in late 2020, and it now sits around the level of a current entry-level desktop card such as an RTX 4060 or RTX 5060 in raster games.

In practice, most PS5 games target 4K output on a TV but do not render natively at 4K. They use dynamic resolution or upscaling, typically rendering somewhere between 1080p and 1440p in performance modes and higher in quality modes. That is the right frame of reference for the PS5 GPU: comfortable at 1080p and 1440p, and dependent on upscaling for 4K.

The 10.28 TFLOPS number is useful against other RDNA 2 chips, such as the Xbox Series X at about 12.1 TFLOPS, but not against NVIDIA cards or newer AMD designs. RDNA 3 and NVIDIA's recent cards count throughput differently, so a card with a much higher TFLOPS figure can perform only a little better. Use game tests, not TFLOPS, to compare across brands.

sections.h: PS5 GPU PC Equivalent: AMD, NVIDIA and Intel
body: Because the PS5 uses RDNA 2, the cleanest match is the desktop card with the same number of compute units: the Radeon RX 6700, the 10 GB model, which also has 36 RDNA 2 compute units. It boosts higher and adds an Infinity Cache the PS5 lacks, but has a narrower 160-bit bus at 320 GB/s against the PS5's 256-bit bus at 448 GB/s. On paper the two land close together.

On the NVIDIA side, the widely reported match is an RTX 2070 Super, which also has 448 GB/s of memory bandwidth. Side-by-side tests of the same games on PS5 and PC, such as those published by Digital Foundry, generally place the PS5 around a 2070 Super, sometimes reaching RTX 2080 level in a well-optimized port. Roughly means within about 10 percent on average. For how these cards line up against each other, use the [AMD vs NVIDIA GPU equivalents chart](/amd-vs-nvidia-gpu-equivalents/).

sections.h: Which Current Graphics Cards Match the PS5 GPU?
body: In today's lineup, an [RTX 4060](/gear/rtx-4060/) or [Arc B580](/gear/arc-b580/) roughly matches or slightly beats the PS5 GPU in raster, and the [RTX 5060](/gear/rtx-5060/) is a little faster again. All three add DLSS or XeSS, which usually look sharper than the upscaling most PS5 games use. The [RX 6600](/gear/rx-6600/) is somewhat slower than a PS5, and the [RX 6700 XT](/gear/rx-6700-xt/) a little faster.

With ray tracing on, the PS5 drops closer to an RTX 2060 Super or RTX 3060, because its RDNA 2 graphics have the same limited ray-tracing hardware as the RX 6000 series. Current NVIDIA cards pull further ahead in heavy RT.

Memory is the catch. The PS5 gives games roughly 12 to 13.5 GB of its 16 GB pool, and ports built around that pool can ask for more than 8 GB of video memory on PC at high textures. The RTX 4060 and RTX 5060 have 8 GB, so a 12 GB B580 or a 16 GB card such as the [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/) matches the PS5 experience more reliably. See [VRAM](/glossary/vram/) for why.

sections.h: What About the PS5 Pro GPU?
body: The PS5 Pro has a different, bigger GPU: 60 compute units, 576 GB/s of memory bandwidth and Sony's PSSR upscaling, with rendering Sony rates up to about 45 percent faster than the PS5. It lands roughly at an RX 7700 XT, between an RTX 4060 Ti and an RTX 4070. The [PS5 Pro GPU equivalent](/ps5-pro-gpu-equivalent/) page covers it in full.

sections.h: What CPU Does the PS5 Have?
body: The GPU shares its chip with an 8-core, 16-thread AMD Zen 2 CPU at up to 3.5 GHz, with a smaller L3 cache than desktop Zen 2. It performs roughly like a Ryzen 7 3700X held to lower clocks, or a Ryzen 7 4700G, and in games it lands closer to a Ryzen 5 3600. In Intel terms, that is roughly a Core i5-10400F to i7-10700 for gaming.

Any current desktop CPU is much faster. A [Ryzen 5 7600](/gear/ryzen-5-7600/) or [Ryzen 7 5700X3D](/gear/ryzen-7-5700x3d/) comfortably beats it, which matters in games locked to 30 or 60 fps on console by the CPU rather than the GPU. Check any CPU and GPU pairing with the [bottleneck calculator](/tools/bottleneck-calculator/).

sections.h: PS5 GPU vs Xbox Series X and Steam Machine
body: The PS5 and Xbox Series X have GPUs from the same RDNA 2 generation. The Series X has more compute units (52) at a lower fixed clock, about 12.1 TFLOPS against the PS5's 10.28, and performs roughly like an RTX 2080; the PS5's higher clock lets it match or win in some games. See [Xbox Series X GPU equivalent](/xbox-series-x-gpu-equivalent/) for that breakdown.

Valve's Steam Machine has a newer RDNA 3 GPU but only 28 compute units, and lands roughly at an RX 6600 XT by its specs, a step below the PS5 in GPU power but well ahead in CPU power. The [Steam Machine GPU equivalent](/steam-machine-gpu-equivalent/) page covers it, and the [console GPU equivalents chart](/console-gpu-equivalents/) puts every console, handheld and older generation in one table.

sections.h: What PC Has a GPU Like the PS5?
body: A PC that matches or slightly beats a PS5 in most games needs a GPU at RTX 4060 level or better, a 6-core CPU from the last few years, and 16 GB of system RAM. With new parts, that means an RTX 5060 or Arc B580 with a Ryzen 5 7600. For PS5 ports with heavy textures, the 12 GB B580 or a 16 GB card is the safer pick than an 8 GB one. See [RTX 5060 vs Arc B580](/compare/rtx-5060-vs-arc-b580/) for that trade-off.

mistakes: 10.28 TFLOPS on RDNA 2 does not equal 10.28 TFLOPS on an NVIDIA or RDNA 3 card. Newer designs count throughput differently, so use the RDNA 2 card with the same compute units, then game tests, to match the PS5.
Thinking the PS5 has a separate graphics card
The PS5's GPU is part of one custom AMD chip with the CPU, and both share 16 GB of GDDR6. There is no removable or upgradeable graphics card inside.
Assuming the Slim or Digital Edition has a weaker GPU
The PS5 Slim and both Digital Editions use the same 36-CU GPU as the original PS5. The PS5 Pro is the only model with a different, faster GPU.
Matching the PS5 with an 8 GB card for big ports
PS5 games can use roughly 12 to 13.5 GB of memory. On PC, ports built for that pool ask for more than 8 GB of VRAM at high textures, so a 12 GB or 16 GB card matches the PS5 experience more reliably.
Most PS5 games reach 4K output with dynamic resolution or upscaling. Compare the PS5 GPU to desktop cards at 1440p with upscaling, not native 4K results.
bottomLine: The PS5 has a custom AMD RDNA 2 GPU with 36 compute units at up to 2.23 GHz, 10.28 TFLOPS, sharing 16 GB of GDDR6 at 448 GB/s with an 8-core Zen 2 CPU. Every PS5 model except the Pro uses it. On PC it is roughly an RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super, and an RTX 4060, RTX 5060 or Arc B580 matches or slightly beats it today; prefer 12 GB or more of VRAM to match its memory pool. The PS5 Pro's bigger 60-CU GPU has its own page.

faqs.q: What GPU does the PS5 have?
faqs.a: A custom AMD GPU based on RDNA 2, built into the same chip as the CPU. It has 36 compute units at up to 2.23 GHz for 10.28 TFLOPS, and shares 16 GB of GDDR6 at 448 GB/s. On PC it is roughly an RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super.

faqs.q: Is the PS5 GPU made by AMD or NVIDIA?
faqs.a: AMD. Both the GPU and the CPU are AMD designs, combined in one custom chip for Sony. The GPU uses RDNA 2, the same architecture as the Radeon RX 6000 series and the Xbox Series X.

faqs.q: How powerful is the PS5 GPU?
faqs.a: About as powerful as a desktop RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super, or a current RTX 4060 in raster games. That is comfortable at 1080p and 1440p, and most PS5 games reach 4K output with dynamic resolution or upscaling.

faqs.q: How many TFLOPS is the PS5?
faqs.a: 10.28 TFLOPS, from 36 RDNA 2 compute units at up to 2.23 GHz. The Xbox Series X is about 12.1 TFLOPS. TFLOPS only compare fairly within the same architecture, so use them alongside game tests.

faqs.q: How much VRAM does the PS5 have?
faqs.a: The PS5 has no separate VRAM. Its 16 GB of GDDR6 at 448 GB/s is shared between the CPU and GPU, and games get roughly 12 to 13.5 GB of it, with the rest reserved for the system.

faqs.q: Does the PS5 Slim have the same GPU as the original PS5?
faqs.a: Yes. The PS5 Slim and the Digital Editions use the same 36-CU RDNA 2 GPU at up to 2.23 GHz, so games perform the same. Only the PS5 Pro has a different, larger GPU.

faqs.q: Does the PS5 GPU support ray tracing?
faqs.a: Yes. RDNA 2 adds hardware ray tracing, with one ray accelerator per compute unit. With ray tracing on, the PS5 performs closer to an RTX 2060 Super or RTX 3060 than to an RTX 2070 Super.

faqs.q: What CPU does the PS5 have?
faqs.a: An 8-core, 16-thread AMD Zen 2 CPU at up to 3.5 GHz, on the same chip as the GPU. In games it lands near a desktop Ryzen 5 3600; any current desktop CPU is much faster.
